value.account:
CHANGED
- State: RunState.result_persistence_profile (omitted when None, validated at construction/from_dict/StateManager.initialize, load never rewrites); initialize(..., result_persistence_profile=). New StateManager methods begin_eligible_pure_visit / reuse_interrupted_eligible_pure_visit / settle_eligible_pure_success / settle_eligible_pure_failure (each one state_transaction; the call-frame manager has equivalents). The shared logic lives in pure_result_replay_progress.py (witness, exact shell, classify_pure_replay_progress, apply_* helpers).
- Selection: `orchestrator run` (compiled .orc) and `resume --force-restart` pass the profile; force-restart no longer writes merged observability into the source run (the source state.json stays byte-identical; the new root gets the observability). calls.py selects it for fresh, non-iteration (step_name_override is None), frontend_kind == workflow_lisp child frames. call_frame_state.py: load_existing_call_frame_read_only; a frame without a mapping `state` raises ValueError('existing call-frame state ...') before mkdir/persist.
- Index (pure_result_replay_index.py + _documents.py): derive_pure_result_replay_index. Eligible = workflow_lisp pure_projection, not loop-owned or on a control-flow cycle (Tarjan), no publishes/consumes. Refs are parsed to typed addresses (WorkflowInput/NodeResult/BlockOutput/LoopOutput/CallOutput) per scope (root/self/parent levels from lexical_scope); documents are walked with the declared type, including inactive union members; malformed refs, '${' text, cycles, duplicate/mismatched projection identity and cross-frame refs raise dependency_index_invalid; scope mismatch carries expected_scope/actual_scope.
- Runtime (pure_result_replay.py, _scans.py): PureReplayRuntime with witness, record_full_result, replay_node, resolve/value_for_state_address, required_node_ids_for_boundary (seeds = every address read by the nodes at/after the boundary plus workflow outputs, found by a generic dataclass/ref scan), audit_boundary_leaves, overlay_active_state, audit_persisted_surfaces (steps / pure_bundle / private_artifact_versions / checkpoint_record / restore_payload conflicts, other frames ignored). Cache hits are revalidated against the exact shell or exact active row.
- Executor: runtime built in execute() for profiled states; on resume the persisted-surface audit (profile_conflict is raised) and progress audit (fail-closed state with error.type pure_result_replay_unavailable) run before the prologue; leaves are audited and required pure values replayed (bundle-free execute_pure_projection over the overlay) after the single restart determination and before the loop. In the loop an eligible node opens its visit atomically (or reuses an interrupted one) before any guard, and _persist_step_result settles through OutcomeRecorder(eligible_pure_settlement=witness): shell on disk, full row in memory. Restart boundary is determined once and passed to ResumePlanner.determine_default_resume_decision(restart_node_id=...). Provider observation manager is now created at execute() start and closed once (two old tests that asserted construction-time creation were updated).
- Checkpoints: emit_runtime_shadow_record skips eligible points, capture_restore_payload omits eligible-sourced bindings, default resume excludes eligible points from nearest-prior selection and adds the VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY zero-record case (otherwise FAIL_CLOSED lexical_default_resume_prior_boundary_not_restorable under the profile).
- Docs: specs/state.md section 'Derived Pure-Result Persistence Profile'. Tests: tests/test_derived_pure_replay_{state,index,runtime,resume,cli}.py (54 tests, behavioural).

VERIFICATION: full `pytest tests -n 4`: 10773 passed, 138 failed; the same 138 fail on the untouched baseline (environment: tmux, missing nanoBragg, AF_UNIX path length, etc.) and none is new.

ALTERNATIVES / DECISIONS
- Considered replaying every derived_complete node on resume (simpler, safer against missed consumers); kept required-only to match the spec, after which a generic scan of whole IR nodes (not just execution_config) was needed - the watchdog test caught branch-guard predicates reading a pure result.
- Considered a separate execution path for eligible nodes in the step loop; instead a single begin hook at the top plus a settlement hook in _persist_step_result covers all pre-visit skip/failure paths.
- Made _execute_step_loop's restart argument optional and kept _determine_resume_default_resume_decision(state) one-argument (restart passed through an attribute) so existing patched seams keep working.
- Module split (index/documents/progress/scans) to stay near the 500-line guideline.

NOT COVERED / RISKS
- classify_pure_replay_progress returns the string 'progress_witness_invalid' rather than raising (spec wording read as a return value); load_existing_call_frame_read_only returns a RunState, not a dict.
- Hidden-test-facing signatures I had to guess: evaluate_node(node, overlay_state) -> step-result mapping; resolve_bundle_path receives a str subclass carrying node_id/step_id/presentation_key.
- A failed (durable_failure_skip) eligible pure step cannot be retried on resume (second visit rejected -> run fails); resuming a fully complete profiled run through execute(resume=True) with no restart node re-walks from the first node and trips the single-visit check.
- Iteration-owned detection relies on step_name_override being set only by nested loop execution. Child-frame replay is exercised only through the watchdog resume test, not a dedicated test. No dashboard/monitor/report changes for shell rows.
- No commit was made.
value.summary: Added the derived_pure_replay.v1 persistence profile: eligible Workflow Lisp pure steps persist only an exact value-free completion shell and resume re-derives their values in memory; the full suite shows no new failures against baseline.
